# Assignment 1

## What is the kernel trick?

The kernel trick is about working with non-linear transformations to higher
dimensions when the data is not linearly separable in the input space.
Transforming data in this way can be expensive. Therefore, if the data
enters the model only as the transformed counterpart, the output scalar
from multiplying to transformations together can be calculated directly.
In this case, the expensive transformation can be avoided. The method that 
allows for this behavior is called the kernel trick. It uses a so-called
kernel function to calculate the result without lifting the input data to
the higher dimension. There exists a set of kernels that follow the given
criteria that can be chosen arbitrarily. [p. 194-195]
